theory.title: Loop invariants and induction
theory.reasoning: State an invariant strong enough to establish the postcondition, prove initialization, preservation and exit, and keep representability of every intermediate as a separate obligation.

bindings.rejects: A final mathematical sum or loop invariant is mistaken for representable intermediates or termination.
bindings.reasoning: Staged prefixes: at step k, staged[0..k) are representable prefixes; [INT_MAX,1,-1] rejects before addition although its final sum fits.

bindings.rejects: Any true loop property is sufficient as an invariant.
bindings.reasoning: Derive 0<=i<=n and acc=sum(a[0..i)) with 0<=acc<=10i; show that acc<=40 is true but cannot establish the final sum.

bindings.rejects: Testing n in 0..4 is an inductive proof of arbitrary length.
bindings.reasoning: Prove initialization, preservation and exit for the summing loop, then delete the increment and name the exact failing obligation.

theory.title: Termination measures and resource bounds
theory.reasoning: Exhibit a nonnegative measure that strictly decreases on every back edge of the actual code under admitted input, and derive the resulting operation and stack bounds.

bindings.rejects: A loop that usually terminates has a proof of progress.
bindings.reasoning: Half-open lower_bound with hi-lo as the decreasing measure on empty, singleton and all-equal arrays.

bindings.rejects: A loop bound stated in English proves termination of the actual code.
bindings.reasoning: Use n-i as a variant, derive n reads, n adds and constant stack, and show how unsigned underflow invalidates a careless variant.

theory.title: Recurrences for divide-and-conquer work and depth
theory.reasoning: Write the work and depth recurrences from the implemented split, including uneven halves and adversarial partitions, and solve each separately rather than quoting an average-case class.

bindings.rejects: Bounded recursion alone gives O(n log n) work.
bindings.reasoning: Smaller-side recursion bounds the depth recurrence while an adversarial pivot still yields the quadratic work recurrence W(n)=W(n-1)+n-1 without a fallback.

bindings.rejects: A randomized pivot alone gives a deterministic worst-case bound.
bindings.reasoning: With a depth budget the combined bound is partition work before fallback plus the heap-sort bound; the expected-case recurrence of a randomized pivot is not a worst-case bound.

bindings.rejects: treats odd n as equal halves
bindings.reasoning: Top-down stable merge: W(1)=0 and W(n)=W(ceil(n/2))+W(floor(n/2))+n-1, so W(7)=14 with recursion depth 3, not n log2 n.

theory.title: Aggregate, accounting and potential arguments
theory.reasoning: Charge copies to growth with a potential function, keep the initial potential in the telescoping sum, and separate the amortized sequence bound from single-operation latency, failed attempts and variable copy weights.

bindings.rejects: An empty-state proof is reused for a negative or nonzero initial potential.
bindings.reasoning: Phi=2*live-capacity from live=5, capacity=8 through the next growth; live=1, capacity=8 starts negative.

bindings.rejects: Amortized constant append guarantees constant per-call latency and stable addresses.
bindings.reasoning: Appends 1..8 with capacities 1,2,4,8 copy 1+2+4=7 old elements, while one append can move the whole prefix and invalidate borrows.

bindings.rejects: Amortized constant insertion implies bounded allocator latency, destructor time or response time.
bindings.reasoning: Variable-size deep copies change the copy weights of the doubling proof; the guarantee is deterministic over the sequence, not probabilistic, and excludes allocator latency.

theory.title: Greedy choice and exchange arguments
theory.reasoning: Prove that exchanging the first choice of an optimal solution for the greedy choice preserves feasibility and value, and falsify plausible alternative rules with small counterexamples.

bindings.rejects: Choosing earliest start or shortest duration is always optimal.
bindings.reasoning: Intervals [0,3),[1,2),[2,4),[3,5): earliest finish yields a maximum compatible set of two; the exchange preserves feasibility.

theory.title: Dynamic-programming state and recurrence design
theory.reasoning: Define what each state represents, which prior states it depends on, the base cases and the evaluation order, then show that memory reduction preserves those dependencies.

bindings.rejects: A recurrence can omit whether the current item was already used.
bindings.reasoning: Bounded 0/1 knapsack over items (2,3),(3,4),(4,5) at capacity 5: each state is an item prefix and capacity; optimum 7 is checked by subsets.

bindings.rejects: Loop direction does not affect0/1item-use semantics.
bindings.reasoning: One item (2,3) at capacity 4: ascending one-row updates reuse the item and give 6; descending updates give the correct 3.

theory.title: Graph traversal and shortest-path correctness
theory.reasoning: Prove discovery uniqueness, that every edge points forward in a returned order, and the settled-set invariant with its nonnegative-weight premise; certificates must be checked against the graph.

bindings.rejects: Dijkstra is correct whenever no negative cycle exists.
bindings.reasoning: 0->A (2), 0->B (5), B->A (-10): the true distance to A is -5, so settling A at 2 is wrong without any negative cycle.

bindings.rejects: Any DFS output list is a topological order.
bindings.reasoning: Every DAG edge points forward in the returned order; adding 3->0 must produce an explicit cycle failure.

bindings.rejects: Visited only after dequeue never increases pending work.
bindings.reasoning: Mark discovery at enqueue on the diamond with a back edge so each vertex is admitted once.

theory.title: Expected cost and probabilistic guarantees
theory.reasoning: Name the pivot, hash or height model behind an expected bound, separate it from deterministic worst cases, and construct the adversarial or saturated input it does not cover.

bindings.rejects: Ordinary quickselect has deterministic linear worst-case cost.
bindings.reasoning: Expected linear work holds only under the stated pivot model; an adversarial partition sequence is quadratic.

bindings.rejects: A probability formula is a per-query guarantee for arbitrary fixed hashes.
bindings.reasoning: A saturated membership filter answers every query positively; the no-false-negative property holds only without deletion or corruption.

bindings.rejects: Low live load factor implies short probes regardless of tombstones.
bindings.reasoning: Live and occupied-or-deleted counts diverge after deletion; expected probe bounds depend on both and on the hash assumption.
